title: Birthday Confetti Cupcakes
shortDescription: Funfetti cupcakes with a classic vanilla swirl, ready in 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake time.
description: These cupcakes taste like a birthday party in cake form. I loaded the batter with rainbow sprinkles so every bite has a pop of color and crunch. The classic vanilla swirl on top keeps things simple, so the sprinkles inside stay the star of the show. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen to get the crumb soft but sturdy enough for kids to grab at a party. A final shower of sprinkles on the frosting makes them look festive without any fancy piping skills.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Add flour mixture and milk in three additions, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
Fold in 1/2 cup rainbow sprinkles by hand. Do not overmix or the batter turns gray.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat 1 cup butter until pale and fluffy. Add powdered sugar one cup at a time on low speed.
Add heavy cream and beat on high for 2 minutes, until the frosting is smooth and holds a swirl.
Pipe frosting high on each cooled cupcake using a large star tip.
Finish with a shower of rainbow sprinkles on top before serving.
tips: Use jimmies, not nonpareils. Nonpareils bleed color into the batter and turn it muddy.
Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if your kitchen is warm. It pipes taller when firm.
Toss sprinkles with 1 tsp of flour before folding in to stop them sinking to the bottom.
Bake a test cupcake first if you are unsure about your oven. Ovens run hot or cool by 10 to 15 degrees.

faq.question: Why did my sprinkles turn the batter gray?
faq.answer: This happens when you overmix or use nonpareils instead of jimmies. Fold sprinkles in gently with a spatula and stop as soon as they are distributed.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost and add sprinkles the morning of the party for the freshest look.

faq.question: Do the sprinkles melt or bleed during baking?
faq.answer: Jimmies hold their shape and color at 350°F, so you will see clear flecks of color once baked. Nonpareils are more likely to bleed, so avoid them here.

faq.question: Can I turn this into a two layer birthday cake instead?
faq.answer: Yes, double the batter and bake in two 8 inch round pans for about 28 to 32 minutes. Check with a toothpick and cool fully before frosting.

conclusion: These cupcakes are my go to for any birthday, big or small. The sprinkles inside are the fun surprise, and the classic swirl keeps them easy to make even on a busy week.
